# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 44 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_044_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 44

**1** Jesus said: "Whoever blasphemes against the Father will be forgiven, and whoever blasphemes against the Son will be forgiven.

**2** But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either on earth or in heaven."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Blasphemes"** — LOGOS/EMET preferred over PNEUMA's "speaks against." *Jiōua* = to blaspheme; the technical religious term for profaning the divine should be preserved.

**"On earth or in heaven"** — LOGOS/EMET preferred over PNEUMA's "in this world or in the next." The Coptic *kah/tpe* = earth/heaven (spatial), not this-age/next-age (temporal).

**Synoptic Parallels:**
- Matt 12:31-32: "Every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven. And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven"
- Mark 3:28-29: "All sins will be forgiven the children of man, and whatever blasphemies they utter; but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness"
- Luke 12:10: "And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but the one who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven"

Thomas's version is the most elaborated: it distinguishes Father, Son, and Holy Spirit separately, with only the Spirit's blasphemy unforgivable. This represents a more developed trinitological framing than the Synoptics.
